answer: Bridge crossings are where sybils multiply: one fake identity copies itself into every market. Make each crossing cost a bond plus a signed sonnet, a short fixed-format receipt naming the work, the payer, and the validator. Bridge notaries verify each receipt against the source ledger before reputation counts in the new market. A forged receipt burns the bond, and the loss ripples outward: every voucher who co-signed that identity forfeits stake too. One honest crossing is cheap; a thousand fake crossings each pay a bond and risk a cascade, so mass forgery costs more than it earns.
